solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Writing of law enforcer delayed by publisher at first

indicators.note: at first points to only the opening letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: a copper is a police officer
the opening letter of publisher
delayed means running late

explanation.surface: A police officer's handwriting held up by a publisher before printing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delayed by' means the late part follows the publisher's initial, rather than being held up by it in time.
explanation.definitionFit: Copperplate is an elegant, flowing style of cursive handwriting, named after engraved copper printing plates.

clue.text: Eg Picasso’s share of profits securing rise for sibling

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast within, so one piece goes inside another
in a down clue a rise means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: a cut is a share of the takings
sib is short for sibling

explanation.surface: Picasso's slice of the earnings being used to help his brother get on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picasso's share' reads as one possessive; the 's is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Picasso co-founded Cubism with Braque, so he is an example of a Cubist painter.

clue.text: Bearer of message presenting a one-sided view?

blocks.note: first meaning: a card sent through the post carries a written note
second meaning: a card with a scene printed on only one face

explanation.walkthrough: 'One-sided view' sounds like bias; it is literally a view printed on one side of a card. As an adjective the answer also means prettily idealised.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday card carries a message on the back and a scenic photograph on the front, one side only.

clue.text: Quest for speed

blocks.note: first meaning: a journey undertaken for a purpose
second meaning: promptness, haste

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a search for velocity; 'for' merely joins two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: An expedition is an organised journey with an aim, and the word also means promptness or haste, as in expeditious.

clue.text: Groups of dolphins originally protected by Officers of the Day

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the first letter of the next word is kept
by means next to, so one piece sits beside the other

blocks.note: the first letter of protected
an OD is an Officer of the Day, a military duty officer

explanation.surface: A school of dolphins guarded by the duty officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' seems to belong with dolphins but applies to protected.
explanation.definitionFit: A pod is the collective noun for a group of dolphins or whales swimming together.

clue.text: Ease a former son of Jacob snatched

indicators.note: something snatched is grabbed and held, so the son is taken inside the other word

blocks.note: taken as written
late means former, as in the late chairman
Levi was the third son of Jacob in Genesis

explanation.surface: Comforting someone after one of Jacob's sons was kidnapped.
explanation.walkthrough: The son goes into the 'former' word just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To alleviate is to make suffering or a problem less severe, the verb sense of ease.

clue.text: Ban printers’ unit before pub game

blocks.note: an em is a printers' measure of width
a bar serves drinks
go is the Japanese board game

explanation.surface: Printers barred from a pub game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pub game' looks like one thing, say darts; it is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official prohibition, especially on trade with a country, so it is a ban.

clue.text: Oft-repeated utterance at church he carps frightfully about

indicators.note: something thrown frightfully about is scattered in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: at, CH for church, he and carps, taken together

explanation.surface: Someone at church keeps complaining about the same thing over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the standard abbreviation for church.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchphrase is a saying a person, often an entertainer, uses again and again until it becomes associated with them.

clue.text: Arrive to welcome German with note for board

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: to arrive is to come
mit is the German word for with
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Turning up to greet a German visitor with a note for the board of directors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German with' is a foreign-word device: the German word for with. The insertion goes just before the last letter of the arrive word.
explanation.definitionFit: A board in the sense of a governing body is a committee, a group appointed to manage or decide.

clue.text: He leaves the grain for a moment

indicators.note: to leave is to depart, so those letters go out of the phrase

blocks.note: taken as written: the letters that depart
taken as written
rice is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: A man walks off and abandons the cereal just for a minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He leaves' reads as a man departing; it is an instruction to remove those two letters from the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: In a trice means in an instant, so a trice is a very brief moment of time.

clue.text: Arab, possibly, has house in Home Counties, lucky thing!

indicators.note: in places the dwelling within the region

blocks.note: an Arab is a breed of horse; possibly marks an example
the Home Counties are those around London, in the South East
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: An Arab gentleman with a home near London is fortunate.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the English counties surrounding London, in the South East.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseshoe hung over a door is a traditional good-luck charm, so it is a lucky object.

clue.text: Confusion from astronomer crushing fraudulent scheme

blocks.note: Edwin Hubble, the American astronomer who showed the universe expanding
a bubble is a speculative scheme, as in the South Sea Bubble

explanation.surface: An astronomer exposing a financial swindle causes chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: The South Sea Bubble of 1720 was a notorious fraudulent investment scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Hubble-bubble means a commotion or uproar, a rhyming word for tumult as well as a name for a hookah.

clue.text: Enduring a loud noise — generous about it

indicators.note: about it means going around the thing just mentioned

blocks.note: taken as written
big-hearted, generous
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: Putting up with a racket, and being magnanimous about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The noise is mentioned first in the clue but sits inside the generous word.
explanation.definitionFit: Abiding means lasting or enduring, as in an abiding memory.

clue.text: Get involved, good about leaving fruit

indicators.note: leaving means going away, so those letters depart from the word

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
re means about, concerning
a greengage is a green plum

explanation.surface: Join in, the good stuff about leaving fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: G and RE leave the start of GREENGAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage in something is to take part or get involved in it.

clue.text: Reverse decision: support youth knocked over outside gym

indicators.note: something knocked over ends up upside down, so the word is read backwards
outside says these letters wrap around the following piece

blocks.note: to back is to support
a lad is a youth
PE, physical education, is school gym

explanation.surface: Supporting a teenager who has been knocked down outside the gym makes someone change their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The youth is turned round first, and only then wraps the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: To backpedal is to retreat from a stated position or withdraw a commitment, like pedalling a bicycle backwards.

clue.text: Crummy seaside feature — more like a rough ride!

blocks.note: bum as an adjective means worthless or of poor quality
a pier is a structure jutting out to sea at a resort

explanation.surface: A shabby seaside attraction offering a jolting ride.
explanation.walkthrough: A bum deal is a poor one, so bum can stand for crummy.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumpier ride is rougher and more jolting; the comparative adjective matches the phrase about being more like a rough ride.

clue.text: Having left for river, fetch glitzy jewellery

indicators.note: having one thing for another means one letter is swapped in to replace a different one

blocks.note: L is the usual abbreviation for left
R is the usual abbreviation for river
to fetch is to bring

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a riverside spot to fetch their flashy jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: In BRING, the R (river) is replaced by L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: Bling is slang for showy, ostentatious jewellery and accessories, an informal word from hip-hop culture.

clue.text: Well-built chair finally installed in workplace

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it
something installed in a room is placed inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a study is a room for working in
the final letter of chair

explanation.surface: A solidly made chair has been put into an office.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturdy describes something strongly built and robust, as is a well-built person or piece of furniture.

clue.text: Open note about current opportunity for supplementing income

blocks.note: overt means open, not hidden
I is the physics symbol for electric current
me is a variant spelling of mi, the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An open letter about the chance to earn some extra money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open note' looks like one phrase but splits after Open; 'about' here only places the note beside the current, a loose positional use.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtime is extra hours worked beyond the normal schedule, usually paid, so it is a way of boosting earnings.

clue.text: Malevolent spirit in work unit left family trapped

indicators.note: something trapped is held inside, so the following pieces go within the first

blocks.note: the erg is a unit of work in physics
L is the abbreviation for left
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: A wicked spirit has caught a family in a factory unit.
explanation.walkthrough: The erg is the old CGS unit of work, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: The erlking is an evil elf-king of Germanic folklore who lures children to their deaths, as in Goethe's ballad.

clue.text: Plunge finally breaking Green supporter’s backbone, partly

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word before it
breaking splits the following words apart, so the letter goes inside them

blocks.note: vert is green in heraldry
the last letter of plunge
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A dive breaking the spine of an environmental campaigner.
explanation.walkthrough: Vert is heraldic green. 'Partly' fits the definition: one bone is part of the backbone.
explanation.definitionFit: A vertebra is one of the small bones of the spinal column, so it is part of the backbone.

clue.text: Release Tom from confinement — and give the game away

annotation.answer: LET THE CAT OUT OF THE BAG

blocks.note: first meaning, taken literally: freeing a tomcat from a sack
second meaning: disclose a secret

explanation.walkthrough: A tom is a male cat, so the literal reading frees an animal; the idiom means revealing something that should have stayed secret.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to reveal a secret by mistake, which is exactly giving the game away.

clue.text: Disapproving cry about drink going up? It’s on the house!

indicators.note: about means around, so the cry surrounds the drink
going up in a down clue means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: fie is an old exclamation of disapproval
a common drink

explanation.surface: A tut-tut as drinks prices rise, but this round is free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the house' sounds like a pub's free round; it defines anything given free.
explanation.definitionFit: A freebie is something given without charge, and on the house means paid for by the establishment.

clue.text: Hapless wife made an impression with king

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
R is rex, king
to etch is to engrave a mark

explanation.surface: An unfortunate wife impressed the king.
explanation.walkthrough: The king is named last but goes second; 'with' allows either order.
explanation.definitionFit: Wretched means miserable or unfortunate, the same as hapless.

clue.text: British hooligan hanging around old women’s feast

indicators.note: hanging around something means surrounding it, so these letters wrap the next ones

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
a lout is a rowdy, aggressive man
O is the abbreviation for old
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A yob loiters around a ladies' banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: LOUT wraps O + W to give L-OW-OUT after B.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowout is informal for a lavish, extravagant meal or party where everyone eats their fill.

clue.text: Endlessly badger man requiring new green veg

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the final letter of each word is dropped

blocks.note: brock is an old name for a badger
a man's name

explanation.surface: Nag a man who needs fresh green vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Requiring new' jokes that the shortened name lacks its final N, which is the abbreviation for new.
explanation.definitionFit: Broccoli is a green vegetable with a thick stalk and clustered flower heads.

clue.text: Former actor holding opening of Macbeth to be over the top

indicators.note: holding something means keeping it inside, so one piece is placed within another
the opening of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: ex means former
Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a celebrated Victorian actor-manager
the first letter of Macbeth

explanation.surface: A retired actor hamming it up in the opening of Macbeth.
explanation.walkthrough: Herbert Beerbohm Tree is a crossword regular for 'actor'. TREE holds M: TRE-M-E.
explanation.definitionFit: Over the top means excessive or exaggerated, the same as extreme in its sense of going beyond reasonable limits.

clue.text: Connection I established at first in place to the north

indicators.note: at first keeps only the opening letter of the word before it
in sets these letters within the next word
in a down clue going to the north means reading upwards

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of established
to place is to put

explanation.surface: A link I founded at the outset somewhere up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place' looks like a noun for a location; it is the verb put.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-up is a link or association, for example a commercial partnership between two firms.

clue.text: Put in leafy recess, half of them submit with hesitation

indicators.note: half of a word means only part of it is kept and the rest dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
to bow is to yield or submit
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Instructions to tuck something into a leafy bower, with some reluctant giving in.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of THEM is its second half, EM.
explanation.definitionFit: To embower is to enclose or shelter in a bower, an arbour of leaves and branches.

clue.text: Surviving without managers giving protection from the rain

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the surviving word goes around the other

blocks.note: to weather a storm is to survive it
a board of directors manages a company

explanation.surface: Getting by without bosses gives shelter from the downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking'; here it has its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Weatherboarding is overlapping horizontal planks fixed on an outside wall to shed rain.

clue.text: Promise shown by hero at Harrow

indicators.note: shown by says the letters are on display inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across hero, at and Harrow

explanation.surface: A schoolboy hero at Harrow, the English public school, making a solemn vow.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath is a solemn pledge or vow, a formal promise often sworn before witnesses.

clue.text: Dutiful knight in parliament with recipient of lesser honour

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: an OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, holds an honour below a knighthood
a diet is a legislative assembly, as in Japan
N is knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A knighted MP sitting alongside someone with a lesser award.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess knight is written N because K is taken by the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Obedient means willing to comply with orders, the same as dutiful.

clue.text: Sound measure of beauty, we hear, after start of month

indicators.note: we hear means judge this word by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: Dec I, the first of December, is the start of that month
a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A way of rating someone's good looks, said to come at the beginning of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: The month's start is read as the date Dec 1, with the Roman numeral I. A bel is a real unit of ten decibels, so the sound-alike lands on a genuine word.
explanation.definitionFit: A decibel is the unit used to measure the loudness or intensity of sound.

clue.text: Wrong, turning up without a card

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means reading from the bottom upwards
without here means outside, so the turned word wraps the next piece

blocks.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mistakenly appearing without a card.
explanation.walkthrough: A tort is the legal term for a civil wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarot card is one of a deck used in fortune-telling, so card stands for it.

clue.text: Brainy chap with temperature, sick internally

indicators.note: internally means on the inside, so this piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a man's name
ill means sick
T is the symbol for temperature

explanation.surface: A clever man running a temperature, feeling unwell inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The sickness sits inside the chap's name, just after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliant can mean exceptionally clever or talented, the same sense as brainy.

clue.text: Encroaching female brought up in home where flowers are displayed

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means lifted so it reads upwards
in places the female inside the flower holder

blocks.note: in means at home
a vase holds cut flowers
Vi is a woman's name, short for Violet

explanation.surface: A woman raised in a house full of flower arrangements.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed female goes into the vase before its last letter, after the home word.
explanation.definitionFit: Invasive means tending to spread into and take over areas, the same as encroaching.

clue.text: Bug ready to skip under farm building? That’s novel

indicators.note: to skip is to leap about, so these letters jump into a new order
under in a down clue puts this part below, so after, the next

blocks.note: a barn is a farm building
taken as written

explanation.surface: An insect poised to hop beneath a barn: now that's new!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like 'new'; it is a book, Dickens's 1841 novel of the Gordon Riots.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnaby Rudge is a historical novel by Charles Dickens, so the clue's closing words point to it.

clue.text: Old coach’s daily account written outside bar

indicators.note: written outside means set down around another word, so it surrounds it

blocks.note: a daily or char is a British cleaning woman who comes in daily
AC is the abbreviation for account
to bar is to ban

explanation.surface: A daily record of an old coach company, kept outside the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a daily is a cleaner who comes in each day, also called a char.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc is an early open motor coach used for outings, now an old-fashioned word for a coach.

clue.text: See viper slithering around church entrance initially

indicators.note: slithering suggests something twisting about, so these letters move into a new order
around says the jumbled letters surround the next piece
initially points to the first letter of the word before it

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of entrance
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Spotting a snake sliding about by a church door.
explanation.walkthrough: The snake and the entrance's first letter are mixed together, and that mixture surrounds the church.
explanation.definitionFit: To perceive is to notice or become aware of something, and see is a common synonym.

clue.text: Old Persian ruler’s quiet expression of pleasure

blocks.note: sh is a call for quiet
ah is a sigh of pleasure

explanation.surface: An old Persian king gives a hushed sigh of contentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Shah was the title of the monarch of Iran, formerly Persia, until the 1979 revolution.

clue.text: Author’s session in bookshop cancelled, ending programme?

blocks.note: a signing is an event where a writer autographs copies
an event called off is cancelled

explanation.surface: A writer's book-signing gets called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In bookshop' just sets the scene for the author's session.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcaster signing off closes a programme or transmission with a final announcement.

clue.text: Youth flustered man carrying high-class resin

indicators.note: someone flustered is in a state of agitated confusion, so these letters are mixed up
carrying something means holding it inside

blocks.note: a lad is a youth
taken as written
U means upper-class

explanation.walkthrough: U as upper-class comes from Nancy Mitford's 'U and non-U'. MAN is jumbled to ANM, which holds U.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladanum, or labdanum, is a soft dark gum resin from rockrose shrubs, used in perfumery.

clue.text: Home-buyer increasingly sore ultimately about time restriction

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of the word before it
about means around, so those words wrap the following ones

blocks.note: more and more, increasingly
the last letter of sore
T is the abbreviation for time
a gag is a restriction on speech

clue.text: Bachelor fled, but returned — to have a dip in this?

indicators.note: returned suggests going back the way it came, so the word is read in reverse

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor
fled means ran away
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: A bran tub is a British party game: a tub of bran hiding small prizes, also called a lucky dip.
explanation.definitionFit: At fairs children plunge a hand into a bran tub to pull out a hidden prize, so it is something for a lucky dip.

clue.text: Maturity teachers originally found in a mostly dreary poet

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
originally keeps only the first letter of the word before it

blocks.note: taken as written
dull means dreary
the first letter of teachers
Thomas Hood was an English poet of the 1800s

explanation.surface: Teachers find maturity in a rather boring poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hood, author of 'The Song of the Shirt', is a crossword regular for poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Adulthood is the state of being fully grown, which is what maturity means.

clue.text: Unexpected action in lab loosely relating to plants

indicators.note: something unexpected comes out differently, so these letters take a new order
loosely means not fixed in place, so these letters are free to rearrange

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Surprise goings-on in a laboratory, studying plants in a relaxed way.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanical means concerning botany, the science of plant life.

clue.text: Emotionally stimulated, like Earl Grey sometimes?

blocks.note: first meaning: moved or roused
second meaning: a cup of tea that has been mixed with a spoon

explanation.walkthrough: Earl Grey looks like a person, the aristocrat; here it is the tea, which you may stir.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirred can mean emotionally moved, and also describes a drink that has been mixed with a spoon.

clue.text: He wrote our best love stories oddly adopting new name

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so these letters are set out in an unusual order

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: An author boasts that his stories are the finest love tales.
explanation.walkthrough: The two N's are added to the fodder before the letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish author wrote Treasure Island, Kidnapped and Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde, so he is a man who wrote.

clue.text: One who saves rupees, always pocketing shillings and copper

indicators.note: pocketing means tucking away inside, so the next pieces go within

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for rupees
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever
s was the abbreviation for the old British shilling
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A thrifty person who saves rupees and keeps pocketing small coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saves' looks like money-saving, which the coins support; here it means rescues. The shilling was a pre-1971 British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A rescuer saves people from danger, matching 'one who saves' in the sense of rescue.

clue.text: Sheltered place some seamen once or students set up

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means raised so it reads upwards

blocks.note: part means some
NUS was the National Union of Seamen, now merged, and is the National Union of Students

clue.text: Container for fluid, one not kept regularly inside

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
inside places these letters within the preceding word

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written
the first and third letters of kept

explanation.surface: A vessel for liquid that one person doesn't keep tidily.
explanation.walkthrough: The kept letters go inside the not word after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkpot is a small pot holding ink, a fluid for writing.

clue.text: Act as judge, though initially deprived

a ref is a referee, a sports judge
the first letter of though

explanation.walkthrough: 'Act as judge' reads as one instruction, to referee; it splits into to be and the ref.
explanation.definitionFit: Bereft means deprived of or lacking something, as in bereft of hope.

clue.text: Reportedly recognises trashy paper: one sustains blows

blocks.note: to recognise is to know
a rag is a low-quality newspaper

explanation.definitionFit: A nose-rag is slang for a handkerchief, which takes the blows when a nose is blown.

clue.text: Fellow lessee’s hypocrisy involving books in French

blocks.note: cant is insincere, sanctimonious talk
OT, the Old Testament, is a set of books
en is French for in

clue.text: Resounding effect of Cosmo at first, one-time archbishop

blocks.note: the first letter of Cosmo

clue.text: Course finally eaten in Eastern plane, perhaps?

in places this letter inside the following pieces

blocks.note: the last letter of eaten
E is the abbreviation for eastern
the plane is a kind of tree

explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' suggests an aircraft; it is the tree. N goes inside E + TREE.

clue.text: Warrant Officer imbibing at home, a heavy drinker

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the next piece goes inside

blocks.note: WO is the abbreviation for Warrant Officer
in means at home

explanation.surface: A warrant officer boozing at home, a real soak.
explanation.definitionFit: A wino is someone, often homeless, who drinks large amounts of cheap wine, so a heavy drinker.

clue.text: Eg Ezra’s enclosure for stray dogs

blocks.note: first meaning: the American poet Ezra ...
second meaning: a pen where strays are held

explanation.surface: Ezra keeps a yard for wandering dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: Ezra is the modernist poet Ezra Pound; 'Eg' signals that he is one example of the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A pound is an official pen for strays, and Pound is the surname of the poet Ezra.

clue.text: Allure of former county briefly belonging to us

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so only the start of the name is kept

blocks.note: Glamorgan was a Welsh county abolished in 1974
our means belonging to us

explanation.surface: The charm of an old county that we can call ours.
explanation.walkthrough: Glamorgan, a former county in south Wales, is shortened to GLAM, its usual abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamour is an alluring, attractive charm, so allure is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Councillor in row about old hooped skirt

blocks.note: Cr is the abbreviation for councillor
taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old
a row is a line

explanation.surface: A councillor in a dispute over an old-fashioned skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel; it is a line. 'About' only sets the old letter beside the row, a loose positional use.
explanation.definitionFit: A crinoline is a stiff petticoat or hooped frame worn to make a skirt stand out, fashionable in the Victorian era.

clue.text: Like emblem of Manx people —and like some other races

blocks.note: first meaning: the Isle of Man's symbol is three running legs joined at the hip
second meaning: a sports-day race run with two partners' legs tied together

explanation.walkthrough: 'Races' suggests peoples, following on from the Manx; it means sporting contests.
explanation.definitionFit: The triskelion of three legs is the Manx national symbol, and in a three-legged race pairs run with adjacent legs tied.

clue.text: Boarding-school altercation that may make the feathers fly!

definitions.text: Boarding-school altercation that may make the feathers fly!

blocks.note: surface reading: a serious scuffle between pupils
setter's reading: the idiom for a row is literal, as stuffing bursts from bedding in a dormitory

explanation.walkthrough: 'Make the feathers fly' usually means a heated quarrel; here the feathers are real ones from burst bedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Boarders in dormitories traditionally battle with their bedding at night, and feather stuffing may burst out.
